faqs.question: Should I use आप or तुम for a teacher in Hindi?
faqs.answer: आप, always. Hindi's three-tier तू/तुम/आप system selects आप when the addressee's status is higher than the speaker's, and a teacher is that by definition. तुम is for status equals in a familiar relationship, which a teacher is not, however fond you are of them.

faqs.question: Is it ever okay to say तू to a teacher?
faqs.answer: No. तू is selected when the addressee is taken to belong to a lower social stratum, so using it to a teacher does not read as casual — it reads as an insult. In the Hindi news corpus तू appears 236 times against 12,335 for आप.

faqs.question: What is the difference between गुरुजी, सर and शिक्षक महोदय?
faqs.answer: गुरुजी is warm spoken address from a student, सर and मैडम are the neutral institutional default, and शिक्षक महोदय is formal written address suited to a parent or a group post. गुरुजी returns only 18 hits in a 19.1-million-token news corpus, which is exactly why it sounds spoken rather than official.

faqs.question: Can I call my teacher गुरुजी in a WhatsApp message?
faqs.answer: If you are their student and the message is to them directly, yes. In a class or school group where forty parents and the principal will also read it, आदरणीय शिक्षक महोदय is the safer register because a group message is semi-public.

faqs.question: How long should a Hindi birthday wish for a teacher be?
faqs.answer: Two lines. Across 197 SubhSandesh birthday pages the median personal message ran 96 characters and 106 of the 197 were under 100, so the six wishes on this page were written to 61–78 Devanagari characters. Length is not what makes a teacher wish good — register is.

faqs.question: What should a parent write to their child's teacher in Hindi?
faqs.answer: Name what the child learned rather than praising the teacher's qualities, use मैडम or शिक्षक महोदय, and close on आभार rather than धन्यवाद for the formal register. Keep आप throughout, including in the verb agreement.

faqs.question: Is it safe to post a birthday wish for a teacher in the school WhatsApp group?
faqs.answer: Only an impersonal one. A group is semi-public, so anything specific to you and the teacher belongs in a direct message; the group version should use आदरणीय, a formal title and an honorific optative like रहें instead of anything that reads as a command.

faqs.question: Can I use Google Translate to write a Hindi birthday wish for my teacher?
faqs.answer: Not without a check. Machine translation fails on exactly the thing that matters here — it will hand you a fluent sentence at the wrong pronoun tier with no warning that the register is wrong. Have a fluent Hindi reader look at the line before you send it.

faqs.question: Should I write the wish in Devanagari or Roman letters?
faqs.answer: Devanagari if the teacher reads it comfortably, Roman only if they do not. For a teacher of English or in a non-Hindi-medium school, a Roman transliteration is a puzzle rather than a courtesy and plain English is kinder.

faqs.question: Is a birthday wish for a teacher the same as a Teachers' Day message?
faqs.answer: No. Teachers' Day in India falls on 5 September and is addressed to the profession, so a class or school-wide message is appropriate; a birthday is personal to one teacher and reads better sent to them directly.

faqs.question: What do I write to a teacher who is also my colleague?
faqs.answer: Use the surname plus जी — शर्मा जी — rather than गुरुजी, which between peers reads as sarcasm. Keep आप anyway: colleagues in Indian staff rooms rarely drop it, even when they are friends.

faqs.question: Does the register change if the teacher is younger than me?
faqs.answer: No. In Hindi the institutional role selects the pronoun, not the age gap, so a 24-year-old lab assistant still gets आप from a 40-year-old parent. The title can soften — सर or मैडम rather than शिक्षक महोदय — but the pronoun tier does not move.

# Birthday Wishes for Teacher in Hindi: Getting the Register Right

Birthday wishes for a teacher in Hindi are decided by register before they are decided by wording: आप, never तू, the verb agreeing in the honorific plural, and one of about five titles — गुरुजी, सर, मैडम, शिक्षक महोदय, or the surname plus जी. Length is not the hard part. Across 197 SubhSandesh birthday pages the median personal message ran **96 characters**, and 106 of those 197 came in under 100.

All six wishes below run 61 to 78 characters in Devanagari, so a correct two-line wish is already the normal size — while the pages ranking here publish 120, 150 and 370 of them without saying which register any line is in. What follows: the register rule, a frequency check in a 19,177,172-token Hindi news corpus, and six wishes sorted by who is sending.

## What register means in a Hindi birthday wish

Register is the level of respect a sentence is grammatically locked into. Hindi does not let you sidestep it: the second person forces a choice, and the verb then agrees.

Persian, French and Spanish run a two-way T/V split; Hindi runs a three-way one, set out in [Hadavizadeh and Singh's 2022 study of politeness in Hindi and Persian](http://scf-lsa.info/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/2-Ali-HADAVIZADEH-Rajdeep-SINGH-16-29.pdf) as तू / तुम / आप — you1, you2, you3.

They are blunt about what selects each: तुम for status equals, तू when the addressee is taken to belong to a lower social stratum, आप when their status is higher than the speaker's.

For a teacher that has one answer. आप is not an upgrade you add for warmth — it is the floor, and dropping below it reads not as informal but as an insult.

## आप or तुम for a teacher? 12,335 against 236

I queried the Leipzig Corpora Collection's Hindi news corpus — `hin_news_2011_1M`, a million sentences and 19,177,172 tokens, the only Hindi corpus it serves — for each pronoun.

[आप returns 12,335 hits](https://api.wortschatz-leipzig.de/ws/words/hin_news_2011_1M/word/%E0%A4%86%E0%A4%AA) and its dative आपको another 6,884. तुम returns 750 and तुम्हें 201; तू returns 236 and तुझे 43. That is roughly 52 आप for every तू, and 16 for every तुम.

Two caveats: this is written news prose, which over-represents formal register, and the 2011 material predates आप becoming a party abbreviation — which helps rather than hurts.

That is why this page exists. A wish copied off a 370-item list can be flawless and still land wrong, because nothing tells you which tier it is in.

## गुरुजी, सर, मैडम or शिक्षक महोदय

Same corpus, the title words. गुरु returns 1,103; शिक्षक 710; सर 517; आचार्य 481; टीचर 260; अध्यापक 195; मैडम 192; शिक्षिका 103; गुरुदेव 35; महोदय 33; and गुरुजी just 18.

Read those with the confounds attached: गुरु is inflated because it also means a religious teacher and the planet Jupiter, सर because it also means "head".

गुरुजी at 18 is the honest signal — a spoken address form that barely surfaces in written news, which is why it reads warm rather than official from a student, and wrong in a note from a parent.

What students do inside an institution is more uniform than a 150-item list suggests. In [Soomro's 2023 study of Pakistani English address forms in academic discourse](http://philjournal.ru/upload/2023-2/240-247.pdf), across 252 responses, honorifics were the largest category used to senior university staff at 50.3% — 78 *Sir* and 49 *Madam* — with occupation-based forms at 11.1%. Those were administrative staff, not Indian schoolteachers, so read it as South Asian sir/madam practice.

Direction matters as much as the word. Across sixteen observed classes, [N'Guessan, Kiroua and Ouattara logged 153 address terms from students to teachers and 236 the other way](https://www.revue-akofena.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/38-Ange-Alex-Kouassi-NGUESSAN-Koffi-Julien-KIROUA-Zana-Thimothee-OUATTARA_433-442.pdf): all 153 student tokens carried a title, while teachers used a bare pronoun 92 times and a first name 86 times.

That study is from Côte d'Ivoire. The asymmetry is still the one Hindi encodes grammatically, and a birthday message is not the moment to flatten it.

| Title form | Corpus frequency | Who says it | Characters of the 96-char median |
|---|---|---|---|
| गुरुजी | 18 | school student, warm | 6 |
| सर / मैडम | 517 / 192 | school and college students, peers | 2 / 4 |
| शिक्षक महोदय | 710 / 33 | parent, or a formal group post | 12 |
| नाम + जी (शर्मा जी) | जी at 4,433 | a fellow teacher | 8 |
| गुरु | 1,103 | third-person reference, not address | 4 |

The most respectful options are also the cheapest: शिक्षक महोदय costs twelve of your ninety-six characters, so there is no length excuse for getting the register wrong.

## Six birthday wishes for a teacher in Hindi, by who is sending

The same teacher needs a different wish from a student, a parent and a colleague, because each stands somewhere different relative to them. Each entry gives the sender, the wish, the register markers, and the length.

### 1. From a school student

For a class teacher you see daily. **जन्मदिन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ, गुरुजी। आप हमें हमेशा सही रास्ता दिखाते हैं।** — *Janmadin ki hardik shubhkamnaye, Guruji. Aap hamein hamesha sahi raasta dikhate hain.*

The markers: गुरुजी, the honorific plural दिखाते हैं, and हमें rather than मुझे, which makes it the class speaking. 75 Devanagari characters, 85 in Roman.

### 2. From a college student

For a lecturer or professor: real, but institutional. **जन्मदिन मुबारक हो, सर। आपसे पढ़ना मेरे लिए सौभाग्य की बात है।** — *Janmadin mubarak ho, sir. Aapse padhna mere liye saubhagya ki baat hai.*

सर carries the deference, आपसे holds the tier, सौभाग्य keeps it short of flattery. 61 characters, the shortest here.

### 3. From a parent to their child's teacher

For a card, email or diary note. **जन्मदिन की शुभकामनाएँ, मैडम। मेरी बेटी ने आपसे बहुत कुछ सीखा है — आपका आभार।** — *Janmadin ki shubhkamnaye, madam. Meri beti ne aapse bahut kuchh seekha hai — aapka aabhaar.*

Name the child's learning rather than the teacher's qualities, then close on आभार, the formal register of thanks. 76 characters.

### 4. From a fellow teacher

For a staff-room colleague, where गुरुजी would read as sarcasm. **जन्मदिन की शुभकामनाएँ, शर्मा जी। आपका साथ पढ़ाना सीखने जैसा है।** — *Janmadin ki shubhkamnaye, Sharma ji. Aapka saath padhana seekhne jaisa hai.*

Surname plus जी is the peer-level honorific, and आप stays: colleagues in Indian staff rooms rarely drop it. 63 characters.

### 5. For a class or school WhatsApp group

For the message forty parents and the principal also read. **आदरणीय शिक्षक महोदय, जन्मदिन की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ। आप स्वस्थ और प्रसन्न रहें।** — *Aadarniya shikshak mahoday, janmadin ki hardik shubhkamnaye. Aap swasth aur prasann rahein.*

A group is semi-public, so nothing here is specific to you and the teacher: आदरणीय and शिक्षक महोदय are deliberately impersonal, रहें an honorific optative rather than a command. 78 characters.

### 6. From a former student, years later

For a teacher you have not seen in years. **जन्मदिन की शुभकामनाएँ, सर। आपकी सिखाई एक बात आज भी काम आती है।** — *Janmadin ki shubhkamnaye, sir. Aapki sikhai ek baat aaj bhi kaam aati hai.*

Naming one thing that stuck beats any general tribute, and the register does not relax with time — a 40-year-old still writes आप. 62 characters.

All six average 69 characters in Devanagari, so any fits on a card, in a group post, or as the message on a [shareable birthday page built from a SubhSandesh template](https://subhsandesh.in/templates).

## There is no single "most polite" Hindi phrasing

Pandharipande's 1979 hierarchy, as set out in the Hadavizadeh and Singh paper, ranks Hindi structures most to least polite: passive, simple present, V+past+करना, optative, चाहिए, future imperative, imperative.

Then [Kumar and Dharurkar's 2025 survey in *Bhasha*](https://edizionicafoscari.it/it/edizioni/riviste/bhasha/2025/1/revisiting-passivity-and-politeness-in-selected-in/) asked twenty near-native Hindi speakers with Thethi, Magahi and Angika first languages to rank the same structures. **65% put the passive at the bottom and 70% put the imperative at the top** — the exact inversion.

Twenty speakers from one region is a small sample, and the authors say so. It is still enough to retire the idea of one universally safest Hindi construction, and it explains why a wish that sounds impeccable in Delhi reads stiff in Bhagalpur.

So do not be clever with syntax. Mark the register plainly — आप, honorific plural verb, a title — and keep the sentence simple: those markers travel, the ranking of constructions does not.

## When a Hindi birthday wish is the wrong thing to send

Sometimes no message is the right vehicle. If your teacher does not read Devanagari comfortably — common for a teacher of English, or a non-Hindi-medium school — a Roman transliteration is a puzzle rather than a courtesy, and plain English is better.

Our own numbers argue against over-building. Of the 195 birthday pages that added a quiz, only 28 ever had it played — 14.4% — so a teacher is likelier to read two respectful lines than finish your interactive game.

Birthday pages are also the one thing people open on a laptop: 48.6% of birthday views were mobile against 51.0% site-wide, which matters if the link lands on a staff-room desktop. And 37.9% of birthday creators password-protect the page against 43.9% site-wide — the wrong instinct for a school group, where the message is meant to be read by everyone.

A caution about this page itself: every Devanagari line above is composed, not verified by a native reader. Machine translation fails on exactly what matters here, producing a fluent sentence at the wrong pronoun tier without warning you.

So have a fluent Hindi reader check the line first if the recipient matters. If the wish should sit inside more than a text box, the [SubhSandesh template library](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) takes photos, music and one message.

## Sources

- Leipzig Corpora Collection, Hindi news corpus `hin_news_2011_1M` — 1,000,000 sentences, 19,177,172 tokens, material dated 2011; queried via the Wortschatz API, 2026-08-27.
- Hadavizadeh & Singh (2022), "Leech's Politeness Maxims and Their Hierarchy in Hindi and Persian." *Studii şi cercetări filologice*, 16–29.
- Kumar & Dharurkar (2025), "Revisiting Passivity and Politeness in Selected Indic Languages." *Bhasha* 4(1), 7–30, 1 July 2025.
- Soomro (2023), "Pakistani English Address Forms in Academic Discourse." *Current Issues in Philology and Pedagogical Linguistics* 2023(2), 240–247.
- N'Guessan, Kiroua & Ouattara (2023), "Address forms in Discourse: English Department Students and Teachers." *Revue Akofena*, March 2023, 433–442.

failed.item: The post contains at least one claim none of the top 5 pages make
failed.why: STRUCTURAL — the mandatory language blocker lands here. This post's differentiating claim IS its script content: six composed Devanagari wishes, six transliterations, the आप/तुम/तू tier guidance and the गुरुजी / सर / मैडम / शिक्षक महोदय title ladder. Every one of those strings is machine-generated and unverified, so the claim is not established. No citation can close it — the five sources verify how Hindi honorification works, not that these particular sentences read as natural, correctly diacritised Hindi to a teacher in Lucknow.
